S01.reason: Appeal, parties, retirement issue, High Court remand and Supreme Court disposition are accurately attributed. Actor, property, event and court bindings match the frame.

S02.label: SUPPORTED
S02.reason: Lease date, rent, permitted uses, monthly tenancy and distinct F-9/Moti Bagh properties match the judgment. The landlord, tenant and Government authority are correctly identified.

S03.label: SUPPORTED
S03.reason: The 1974 petition, Suit No. 182, its reported pendency and alleged grounds are accurately stated. Allegations are not promoted to adjudicated facts; E04 and party bindings match.

S04.label: SUPPORTED
S04.reason: The September policy, October commencement, three-month period and distinction between Government servants and statutory persons are supported. The policy authority and reporting court bindings are consistent.

S05.label: SUPPORTED
S05.reason: Retirement, Government residence, notice date, issuing official and threatened consequences are recorded. Conditional charges and eviction are not represented as completed acts; E01/E02 and P02 match.

S06.label: SUPPORTED
S06.reason: Filing, leave application, refusal and eviction decree match the chronology. The three determinations remain attributed to the Rent Controller; issuing and reporting courts are correctly separated.

S07.label: SUPPORTED
S07.reason: All three objections match the tenant's reported submissions: retirement, earlier proceeding and mixed use. Their asserted legal consequences are not misattributed to the Supreme Court.

S08.label: SUPPORTED
S08.reason: The High Court's retirement-based reasoning, reversal and remand to the Rent Controller are correctly attributed. The Supreme Court's contrary interpretation is distinguished; E06 and court bindings match.

S09.label: SUPPORTED
S09.reason: Section 14A conditions, qualifying ownership, allotment, governmental order and accrual language are accurately reconstructed. Conditional entitlement is not converted into independent verification of all inputs.

S10.label: SUPPORTED
S10.reason: The Court adopted the ordinary meaning of 'person', rejected the serving-employee restriction and allowed the appeal. Policy, legislative reasoning and court attribution match.

S11.label: SUPPORTED
S11.reason: The Court acknowledged the narrower policy evidence and understandable High Court view but declined to restrict statutory 'person'. Contrary material is correctly distinguished from the adopted rule.

S12.label: SUPPORTED
S12.reason: Nihal Chand's tentative observation, undecided issue and pre-retirement notice are accurately distinguished from Muttoo's post-retirement notice. No invalid retirement date from the source is repeated.

S13.label: SUPPORTED
S13.reason: The admitted mixed-use lease, DDA residential scheme, different statutory wording and rejection of exclusive residential letting under section 14A are supported. P01 and party bindings match.

S14.label: SUPPORTED
S14.reason: Precedent facts are confined to their own tenancies. The Court expressly reserved the predominantly residential and insignificant professional-use question; no actual activity at F-9 is inferred.

S15.label: SUPPORTED
S15.reason: The tenant's pendency objection, Rent Controller's new-cause reasoning and Supreme Court's independent rejection are recorded. Earlier allegations remain unadjudicated; event and court bindings match.

S16.label: SUPPORTED
S16.reason: Sections 25B(4)-(5), the restricted leave inquiry, its distinction from CPC procedure and the identified section 14A disqualifying facts match the Court's reasoning.

S17.label: SUPPORTED
S17.reason: The Court rejected the stated legal effects of retirement, pendency and mixed use. The account distinguishes reported objections from statutory disqualification and does not claim to reproduce the full affidavit.

S18.label: SUPPORTED
S18.reason: Counsel's proposed incorporation of section 14(1)(e) requirements is accurately attributed and rejected. The Court's treatment of sections 25B, 25C, 14(6) and 14(7) is preserved.

S19.label: SUPPORTED
S19.reason: The five-year transfer restriction and section 25C(1) exception are correctly interpreted. The judgment gives no case-specific acquisition-by-transfer date for F-9.

S20.label: SUPPORTED
S20.reason: Section 25C(2) substitutes two months for six months and applies to section 14A recovery orders. The waiting period is a legal condition, not evidence of actual possession.

S21.label: SUPPORTED
S21.reason: The appellate disposition and each principal adopted rationale match the judgment. The two-month restriction and distinction from independently verified premises or physical delivery are preserved.

S22.label: SUPPORTED
S22.reason: The complete source records ownership, letting and prior Government occupation but supplies no separate title-registration adjudication or precisely dated post-retirement physical occupation finding.

S23.label: SUPPORTED
S23.reason: Both dates and the statutory accrual wording are documented. No separate unique-order-date computation or actual payment of threatened charges is established; the limitation is appropriately qualified.

S24.label: SUPPORTED
S24.reason: The original eviction decree, its reversal, appellate disposition and two-month rule are accurately separated. No physical recovery or surrender date appears in the supplied judgment.

S25.label: SUPPORTED
S25.reason: The supplied R1 computation explicitly records UNKNOWN overall and UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/TRUE inputs. The statement correctly separates those model states from the Supreme Court's holding.

S26.reason: The Court did not adjudicate the earlier petition's allegations or prove section 14(1)(e) elements. Authorized professional use is not treated as actual conduct, and no earlier-case outcome is invented.
